provenance.authoringPolicy: Open-source or original content only; names/aliases do not establish identity; supported position/apparatus/contraction variants remain distinct; no media included. Rewritten instructions and all editable defaults are SpotBot editorial adaptations, not claims by the original provider. Range-of-motion drills and stretching recorded under retiredExercises are excluded from active content and future imports. Yoga identities remain available, including poses with overlapping stretching tags. Loaded/bodyweight strength and foam-rolling recovery are retained. Retirements never redirect to a different movement. Grip-only variants are consolidated when a matching base movement exists; preserve equipment, support, position and movement differences. The 40 unusual exercise entries explicitly retired on 2026-09-17 are excluded by product direction; no inferred replacements. On 2026-09-21 the user approved all 176 explicitly ranked form/setup consolidations, including conditional seated/standing, unilateral, support and range cases. Those approved mappings supersede earlier keep-distinct decisions for those pairs; retain standard identities, useful aliases and optional instructions without rewriting historical workout loads or counts. Other equipment/movement distinctions remain individually reviewed. On 2026-09-21 the user approved all 186 rows of the second simplification review: 102 consolidations into their explicitly listed standards and 84 product-scope removals without replacement. These approved choices supersede prior keep-distinct decisions for those rows. Preserve aliases for consolidations only, optional movement/counting distinctions, and original historical workout identities and prescriptions; alternative apparatus must not become simultaneous requirements. On 2026-09-22 the user explicitly removed Finger Curls, Wrist Roller, Barbell Wrist Curl, and Seated Palms-Down Barbell Wrist Curl without replacements. Their former variants remain excluded; remaining dumbbell and cable wrist curls are unchanged. On 2026-09-22 the user reviewed Round 9 and explicitly removed sixteen named exercises without replacement; their historical identities, reviews, media and spending are preserved. The user also requested the display name Plate Loaded Incline Chest Press for the surviving incline machine, then accepted its selected clip. On 2026-09-29 the requested Smith-machine coverage expansion added reviewed apparatus variants, preserving existing Bulgarian-split-squat and stiff-legged/Romanian-hinge identities and all retirements. No automatic Smith counterparts are inferred for Olympic catches, jumps, landmine pivots, rolling bars, torso twists, overhead squats, overhead triceps extensions or pullovers; these are not straightforward guided-bar substitutions. A drag curl and lying skullcrusher have separately authored rail-compatible execution. Front and box squats remain distinct as in the barbell catalog; ordinary grip and stance options are not duplicated. On 2026-09-29 the user explicitly removed Lower Back-SMR following its unresolved Form Guidance audit concern; retain its retirement identity without replacement or reimport.

duplicateCandidateReviews.reason: Warrior I faces the hips forward in a staggered stance; Warrior II opens the hips and arms sideways.
External and internal band rotation move the forearm outward versus across the abdomen.
Barbell rack loading versus dumbbells at the sides changes required apparatus and load position.
Flat and incline Smith bench presses have distinct supported torso angles.
Supported heel-to-toe walking uses a wall; the original walk is unsupported.

Compared full current instructions after the approved barbell display-name generalization: the cable exercise defaults to a rope on a low pulley with cable resistance behind the head; the barbell exercise holds and lowers a free straight bar overhead. Their required apparatus, resistance direction, setup and load records differ. This pair was not approved for consolidation. Retain the cable and barbell standards separately.
Decline and incline Smith presses use opposite bench angles; names were standardized, movements remain distinct.
The existing Smith squat, including its feet-forward chair-squat option, has no physical seat. The box squat requires a stable box and a supported braced pause.
Conventional Smith deadlifts grip outside a hip-width stance; sumo deadlifts use a wide stance and inside-leg grip, matching the separately retained barbell movements.
Decline and flat Smith presses use distinct supported torso angles.

starterWorkouts.name: Dumbbell Full Body
starterWorkouts.description: A simple squat, dumbbell row, and dumbbell shoulder press session. Choose loads that allow controlled repetitions.

starterWorkouts.name: Barbell Foundations
starterWorkouts.description: Squat, press, hinge, and row with a barbell, bench, and rack. Use familiar technique and controlled working sets.

starterWorkouts.name: Band Strength Basics
starterWorkouts.description: A portable full-body band session. Use a secure anchor where the exercise requires one.

starterWorkouts.name: Steady Walking
starterWorkouts.description: One continuous outdoor walking interval. Record time, distance, or both at a comfortable steady pace.

starterWorkouts.name: Gym Cardio Sampler
starterWorkouts.description: Three steady machine intervals with easy transitions. Adjust the effort to keep breathing controlled.

starterWorkouts.name: Seated Cardio Rhythm
starterWorkouts.description: Short seated intervals using a stable chair. Choose a comfortable pace and rest between movements.

starterWorkouts.name: Bodyweight Foundations
starterWorkouts.description: Accessible pushing, standing, hips, and trunk control with a wall and stable chair.

starterWorkouts.name: Standing and Supported Bodyweight
starterWorkouts.description: A beginner sequence with a bench, chair, stable box and pull-up bar; use leg assistance for the pull-up.

starterWorkouts.name: Bar and Core Strength
starterWorkouts.description: Pulling and support work for people already comfortable on a pull-up bar and parallel bars.

starterWorkouts.name: Chair Yoga Foundations
starterWorkouts.description: A seated yoga sequence using one stable chair. Use comfortable ranges and the editable hold targets.

starterWorkouts.name: Standing Yoga Balance
starterWorkouts.description: A deliberate standing sequence with longer holds and side changes. Use comfortable ranges and pause between poses as needed.

starterWorkouts.name: Floor Yoga Unwind
starterWorkouts.description: Seated and floor poses ending in quiet rest. Use a wall for the supported leg position.

starterWorkouts.name: Pilates Floor Foundations
starterWorkouts.description: Begin with small leg movements and supported trunk work. Keep the pelvis quiet and the breathing continuous.

starterWorkouts.name: Chair Pilates Strength
starterWorkouts.description: Controlled seated knee extensions and heel raises with a stable chair.

starterWorkouts.name: Pilates Side-Line Series
starterWorkouts.description: Side-lying clamshells, leg lifts and controlled front-to-back kicks.

starterWorkouts.name: Supported Balance Basics
starterWorkouts.description: Start beside a stable chair in a clear area. Use its support for the single-leg hold.

starterWorkouts.name: Supported Walking Balance
starterWorkouts.description: Practice controlled steps beside a clear wall, using light hand support whenever needed.

starterWorkouts.name: Single-Leg Balance Control
starterWorkouts.description: Static holds followed by small reaches. Return both feet to the floor between efforts as needed.

starterWorkouts.name: Low-Impact Conditioning
starterWorkouts.description: Standing rhythm, squat-to-rise, and controlled boxing without jumping.

starterWorkouts.name: Bodyweight Conditioning
starterWorkouts.description: A mix of floor and traveling work in a clear space, with recovery after each set.

starterWorkouts.name: Ropes and Sled Circuit
starterWorkouts.description: Alternate battle ropes and sled pushes. Record the time, distance, and external load for each station.
